foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of bread and rolls having wheat as main ingredient. Different sub-types, including those with added minor ingredients, belong to this group. However breads containing considerable proportions of wheat and rye are not included in this group and are listed under A005M 'Mixed wheat and rye bread and rolls'.

foodex2_name: Wheat bread and rolls, white (refined flour)
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of bread and rolls made with refined wheat flour (i.e. containing very little or no bran).

foodex2_name: Wheat bread and rolls, white with maize
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of bread and rolls made with refined wheat flour (i.e. containing very little or no bran) with addition or minor amounts of maize.
The group includes any type of bread and rolls made with wheat flour containing moderate amounts of bran (semi-brown wheat flour).

foodex2_name: Wheat bread and rolls, brown or wholemeal
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of bread and rolls made with wheat flour containing high proportion of bran or wholemeal (brown or wholemeal wheat flour).
The group includes any type of bread having rye as main ingredient. The presence of wheat flour is considered almost negligible.

foodex2_name: Rye bread and rolls, refined flour
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of bread and rolls made with refined rye flour (i.e. containing very little or no bran).
The group includes any type of bread and rolls made with rye flour containing high proportion of bran or wholemeal (brown or wholemeal rye flour).

foodex2_name: Bread and rolls with special ingredients added
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Bread and rolls with special ingredients added.
The group includes any type of bread and rolls containing considerable proportions of different cereals.

foodex2_name: Mixed wheat and rye bread and rolls
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of bread and rolls containing considerable proportions of wheat and rye.

foodex2_name: Rye-wheat bread and rolls, refined flour
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of bread and rolls containing considerable proportions of wheat and rye refined flours (i.e. containing very little or no bran).
The group includes any type of bread and rolls containing considerable proportions of wheat and rye wholemeal flours.

foodex2_name: Multigrain (not only rye-wheat) bread and rolls
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Multigrain (not only rye-wheat) bread and rolls, i.e. breads containing considerable proportions of different cereals. Wheat breads with minor amounts of another cereal are not included in this term and they are listed under A004X 'Wheat bread and rolls'.

The group includes any type of Crackers (i.e. grain flour dough layered and baked in form of salty biscuits) and dry breadsticks. Water crackers, soda crackers, biscuit crackers are included in this group.
The group includes any type of crisp bread based on rye flour containing high proportion of bran or wholemeal (brown or wholemeal rye flour).
The group includes any type of crisp bread based on refined rye flour (i.e. containing very little or no bran).
The group includes any type of crisp bread based on wheat flour containing high proportion of bran or wholemeal (brown or wholemeal wheat flour).
The group includes any type of crisp bread based on refined wheat flour (i.e. containing very little or no bran).
The group includes any type of Rusk, which is a sweet sliced bread browned in an oven.
The group includes any type of Rusk based on refined flour (i.e. containing very little or no bran), e.g. fette biscottate.
The group includes any type of Rusk based on flour containing high proportion of bran or wholemeal.
The group includes any type of Pizza base, partially or totally cooked. These products are normally pressed after leavening and they partly resemble unleavened bread.
The group includes any type of Traditional unleavened or flat breads marketed with different names in different regions.
The group includes any type of Pita bread, a flat bread of Middle Eastern origin also known as Pitta, Arab bread, Lebanese bread or Syrian bread.
The group includes any type of Tortilla or taco, a flat bread traditionally based on maize meal, but nowadays also made from wheat flour.
The group includes any type of Breadcrumbs, including e.g. bread raspings or paniermehl.
The group includes any type of Bread stuffing, i.e. stuffings where bread plays a predominant role or is the main ingredient.
The category includes any type of pasta and similar products, otherwise known in some regions under the name of noodles.
The group includes any type of plain pasta (i.e. not stuffed).
The group includes any type of fresh egg pasta (i.e. pasta including eggs, not dried, normally needing refrigeration).
The group includes any type of Dried pasta (where the moisture content has been reduced to such an extent to allow storage for longer period at room temperature).
The group includes any type of dried pasta containing eggs (where the moisture content has been reduced to such an extent to allow storage for longer period at room temperature).

The group includes any type of dried pasta obtained from durum wheat (where the moisture content has been reduced to such an extent to allow storage for longer period at room temperature), without addition of eggs.
The group includes any type of Gnocchi, i.e. small pasta dumplings, mostly including a considerable proportion of potatoes and other vegetables, mixed in a dough but not as filling/stuffing.
The group includes any type of Glass noodle, i.e. different types of transparent or almost transparent noodles similar in form to regular pasta, mostly spaghetti, made from starch and water.
The group includes any type of Yeast Bread/pizza dough, i.e. yeast-leavened doughs used for production of the pizza base or similar products.
The group includes any type of Fine Yeast sweet dough, i.e. sweet doughs used for production of brioche or similar products risen by yeast fermentation.
The group includes any type of doughs made without using leavening agents. Most often, water provides the structure by evaporating during baking.
The group includes any type of pate brisee, i.e. the dough usually used for making salty or sweet tarts, vegetable pies and similar.
The group includes any type of Cake batter and pre-mixes. However dry pre-mixes are not included in this group.
The group includes any type of laminated dough.

foodex2_name: Suet pastry (pâte a grasse de boeuf) dough
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Suet pastry (pâte a grasse de boeuf) dough, containing beef suet.
The group includes any type of Biscuits and cookies (sweet and semi-sweet).
The group includes any type of sweet plain biscuits, i.e. biscuits without filling, coating or inclusion of pieces of e.g. chocolate or fruit.
The group includes any type of Butter biscuits such as småkage and Danish cookies.
The group includes any type of cocoa powder-based biscuits. This term should not be used for chocolate filled biscuits and biscuits containing pieces of chocolate.
The group includes any type of sweet biscuits based on wheat flour containing high proportion of bran or wholemeal.

foodex2_name: Biscuit with inclusions, filling or coating
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of filled biscuit, i.e. biscuits with inclusions, filling or coating such as American cookies.

The group includes any type of cake, i.e. sweets generally constituted by baked sweet dough/batter and possibly containing creams or fillings of different nature, regardless the size. Individual sized cakes, such as cupcakes are also included in this group. Often a final glazing or icing is also present.

The group includes any type of plain cakes, i.e. cakes mainly constituted of a baked sweet dough. Small cakes such as cupcakes mainly constituted of a baked sweet dough are also included in this group.
The group includes any type of Sponge cake, i.e. a cake based on a particularly aerated and flexible baked product, rich in eggs.
The group includes any type of Cheese cake, i.e. a cake containing a considerable proportion of cheese/cheese-based cream.

The group includes any type of Cream cake, i.e. a cake containing a considerable proportion of a cream. Cakes containing a cheese-based cream are not included in this term and are listed under A00AR 'Cheese cake'.
The group includes any type of Fruit cake, i.e. a cake containing a considerable proportion of fruit.
The group includes any type of Muffins, individual-sized bakery products with or without fillings/inclusions. Cupcakes consisting of a muffin base are also included.
The group includes any type of cakes with a chocolate-based baked part.
The group includes any type of Chocolate cake.
The group includes any type of yeast leavened pastry, i.e. pastries obtained from a yeast leavened dough. In some cases the dough is laminated to improve its structure.

The group includes any type of Buns, i.e. small-sized pastries based on a yeast leavened dough, usually enriched with sugar and butter and sometimes eggs. Savoury variants are also available on the market.
The group includes any type of Croissant, made of a layered yeast-leavened dough with unspecified filling (eventually also without).
The group includes any type of Croissant, filled with chocolate.
The group includes any type of Croissant, filled with jam or similar.
The group includes any type of Doughnuts-berliner, usually consisting of a fried sweet dough. Baked (not fried) variants are also present on the market.
The group includes any type of kringles, typical Scandinavian pastries such as scandinavian pretzel.

The group includes any type of Brioche and similar products (with or without topping-filling). The brioche is usually a yeast-leavened enriched dough based pastry, such as Panettone, Pandoro, Kalacs, Cozonac and Kalac.
The group includes any type of pie and tart based on shortcrust.
The group includes any type of Fruit pie-tart, normally including a thinner layer of cream/custrad, fruit and eventually a sweet aspic topping.
The group includes any type of savoury pie with cheese as characterising ingredient.

The group includes any type of pastry based on a baked laminated dough such as Puff pastry and Danish pastry. The layering process and the fat present between the layers provides a structure made of multiple thin sheets.
The group includes any type of Croissant from puff pastry with unspecified filling (eventually also without).
The group includes any type of Puff-pastry croissant, filled with chocolate.
The group includes any type of Apple strudel.
The group includes any type of strudel with cream or cheese-based cream.
The group includes various pastries not listed elsewhere.
The group includes any type of sweet dumpling.
The group includes any type of Pancakes.

The group includes any type of Scone, i.e. small sweet bread like pastries traditionally consumed at tea time with butter-marmalade. Savoury variations, such as Pogacsa, are also included in this group.
The group includes any type of Waffles.
The group includes any type of Lebkuchen, a honey or pepper cake with different spicing, resembling gingerbread, traditionally related to Christmas.

The group includes any type of Processed maize-based flakes e.g. the corn flakes. Cereal flakes are breakfast cereals usually obtained by soaking-cooking/steaming, pressing, drying and flaking cereal grains/flours mixed with admixture of additional ingredients (e.g. sweeteners). The group includes any type of Processed maize-based flakes.

The group includes any type of Processed oat-based flakes. Cereal flakes are breakfast cereals usually obtained by soaking-cooking/steaming, pressing, drying and flaking cereal grains/flours mixed with admixture of additional ingredients (e.g. sweeteners).

The group includes any type of Processed wheat-based flakes. Cereal flakes are breakfast cereals usually obtained by soaking-cooking/steaming, pressing, drying and flaking cereal grains/flours mixed with admixture of additional ingredients (e.g. sweeteners).

foodex2_name: Muesli and similar mixed breakfast cereals
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Muesli, which is typically produced from mixtures of uncooked rolled cereals, mainly oats, and other breakfast cereals composed by a mixture of grains and possibly other ingredients.
The group includes any type of Mixed breakfast cereals, including mixed muesli, usually made by cereal grains mixed with other ingredients, like raisins, chocolate, nuts and dried fruit.

The group includes any type of Processed flakes made with mixed cereals. Cereal flakes are breakfast cereals usually obtained by soaking-cooking/steaming, pressing, drying and flaking cereal grains/flours mixed with admixture of additional ingredients (e.g. sweeteners).

The group includes any type of Corn semolina based thick soup, such as polenta or mamaliga, i.e. a soup obtained by boiling the semolina with a liquid phase, like milk or water, and adding possibly other ingredients. The product is very often in a salty version.
The group includes any type of Oat porridge in dry form to be diluted with milk or water. The term refers to e.g. ground oatmeal or rolled oat intended to be used for making oat porridge.
The group includes any type of Rice porridge in dry form to be diluted with milk or water. The term refers to e.g. ground rice or rice flakes intended to be used for making rice porridge.
The group includes any type of Cereal bars mixed, i.e. including considerable proportions of other ingredients (e.g. nuts, raisins, etc.).
The group includes any type of mixed cereal-based snacks.

The category covers all raw vegetables and their derivatives, with the exclusion of starchy roots/tubers, legumes (as seeds), nuts, oilseeds and spices. Fruit, though of vegetable origin, is not considered as vegetable. Same for Cocoa, coffee, tea and other vegetable materials for infusions.
The group includes any type of Canned mushrooms.

foodex2_name: Processed or preserved vegetables and similar
foodex2_scope_note: The category includes processed or preserved vegetables, including mushrooms, algae, mosses and lichens. The main processes included are canning, salting, preserving with sugar, drying, fermenting and pickling.
The group includes any type of preserved tomato, whole or pieces.
The group includes any type of Tomato purée.
The group includes any type of preserved concentrated tomatoes.
The group includes any type of Tomato paste or concentrate.

The group includes any type of Pickled / marinated vegetables, i.e. Plant commodities used as vegetables, marinated with acidic and or spiced media. Typical example are some fruiting vegetables in vinegar with herbs and spices.
The group includes any type of Sauerkraut.
The group includes any type of Sweet corn canned.
The group includes any type of dried vegetables.
The group includes dried potato products: non purified products from potato in dried form. Purified starch is in the starch category.
The group includes any type of Potato crisps (also known as chips in American English), made of thin slices of potatoes or potato-based doughs, included those in form of small sticks.
The group includes any type of Roesti, i.e. a potato-based dish originating from Switzerland usually made with grated potato, and possibly other ingredients, and fried.
The group includes any type of Fries, fried starchy root vegetables in form of sticks or fingers.

The group includes any type of Potato boiled. However the use of this term is discouraged because it is inconsistent with the logic of the system and 'boiled potatoes' should be coded by the users as A00ZT#F28. A07GL (i.e. Potatoes, PROCESS=Boiling).
The group includes any type of pan-fried potato.
Oilseeds from the plant classified under the species Arachis hypogaea L., commonly known as Peanuts or Groundnuts.
The group includes any type of Spices (as defined in the list of pesticide regulation).

Spices from the fruits of the plant classified under the species Piper nigrum L., commonly known as Black pepper. On the bases of the time of harvest and the method of processing different kind of peppercorn (e.g. black, green and white) are obtained.
Spices from the fruits of the plant classified under the species Schinus molle L., commonly known as Pink pepper fruit.
The group includes any type of canned or jarred common beans.
The group includes any type of canned or jarred peas.
The group includes any type of canned or jarred chick pea.
The group includes any type of Sesame paste (Tahini) (Sesamus indicum).
The group includes any type of Peanut butter.

The group includes fruits of Olea europaea processed in order to be directly eaten, such as table olives (common olive) ready for consumption. The group includes any type of Table olives ready for consumption.
The group includes any type of processed olives.
The group includes any type of dried vine fruits, such as raisins or sultans or black corinth.

The group includes any type of Jam of fruit and vegetables as defined by EU legislation (Council Directive 2001/113/EC): spreadable preserves of fruit or vegetables or mixtures thereof with sugar and/or syrups, with the exclusiuon of some similar products from citrus fruits (considered under marmalades under specific conditions in Council Directive 2001/113).
The group includes any type of Jam obtained from Strawberries.
The group includes any type of Jam obtained from Apricots.
The group includes any type of Jam obtained from Plums.
The group includes any type of Jam obtained from Mixed fruit.

The group includes any type of marmalade as defined by EU legislation (Council Directive 2001/113/EC): spreadable preserves of citrus fruits following specific conditions according to Directive 2001/113, i.e. a mamrmelade is a mixture, brought to a suitable gelled consistency, of water, sugars and one or more of the following products obtained from citrus fruit: pulp, purée, juice, aqueous extracts and peel. The quantity of citrus fruit used in the manufacture of 1 000 g of finished product must not be less than 200 g of which at least 75 g must be obtained from the endocarp. Citrus spreads not following these contitions are under normal jams.
The group includes any type of Marmalade obtained from Oranges.
The group includes any type of Canned or jarred fruit.
The group includes any type of Canned or jarred Apricot.
The group includes any type of Canned or jarred Sour cherry.
The group includes any type of Canned or jarred Pineapple.
The group includes any type of Canned or jarred Mixed fruit.

The group includes any type of compote of fruit and vegetables, i.e. preparations of fruit made of whole or pieces of fruit in sugar syrup. Fruits are usually cooked in water with sugar and spices. The syrup may be seasoned with vanilla, lemon or orange peel, cinnamon sticks or powder, cloves, ground almonds, grated coconut, candied fruit, or raisins. Similar products may also be prepared with some vegetables.
The group includes any type of Fruit compote obtained from Apple.
The group includes any type of Fruit compote obtained from Pear.
The group includes any type of Fruit compote obtained from Sour cherry.
The group includes any type of Fruit compote obtained from Mixed fruit.
The group includes any type of Mixed dried fruits.
The group includes any type of Fruit salad.

The group includes any type of cured seasoned pork meat (uncooked) made from entire pieces of muscle meat, such as coppa or capocollo or lomo or lonza. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of pork ham, usually made by curing the hind leg of pigs. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Bacon, usually made by curing pig meat. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of cured seasoned poultry meat (uncooked) made from entire pieces of muscle meat. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of cooked cured and/or seasoned meat made from entire pieces of muscle meat. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of cooked cured or seasoned pork meat made from entire pieces of muscle meat. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of cooked pork ham, i.e. cured and cooked hind leg of pigs. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Cooked turkey meat. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Corned turkey. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Sausages, i.e. more or less coarse mixtures of lean meats, fatty tissues and other ingredients, often filled into casings. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Italian-type sausage (Italian sausages), i.e. fresh raw sausages which are usually fried or grilled. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of fresh raw spiced sausages in casings, usually made of finely cut pork, moderately or highly spiced and intended to be cooked. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of fresh bulk sausages, also known as sausage meat, i.e. raw, ground, spiced meat, usually sold without any casing and intended to be cooked.

The group includes any type of Breakfast-type sausage (Breakfast sausage or Country sausage), i.e. a fresh raw sausage made like most sausages of pork, salt and pepper with sage being the dominant spice and intended to be cooked. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Chipolata-type sausage (chipolata), a fresh raw sausage usually grilled. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Fresh bratwurst, i.e. a German sausage which is usually fried or grilled, made of pork or a mixture of pork and veal/beef and highly seasoned. For the cooked variants of bratwurst use the code A026E 'Cooked bratwurst-type sausage'. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Cured unripened raw sausages such as cured spreadable sausages, fermented spreadable sausages and hot smoked spreadable sausages. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Mettwurst-type sausage (Mettwurst), based on cured beef and/or pork, ground and lightly spiced with allspice, ginger, mustard and coriander. Mettwurst is usually smoked and has smooth and spreadable consistency. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Cured ripened raw sausages such as matured sausages or dried sausages or smoked firm sausages. Ripened raw-fermented sausages are uncooked meat products and consist of more or less coarse mixtures of lean meats and fatty tissues combined with salts, nitrite (curing agent), sugars and spices and other non-meat ingredients filled into casings. They receive their characteristic properties (flavour, firm texture, red curing colour) through fermentation processes. Shorter or longer ripening phases combined with moisture reduction (“drying”) are necessary to build-up the typical flavour and texture of the final product. The products are not subjected to any heat treatment during processing and are in most cases distributed and consumed raw. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Salami-type sausage. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Hungarian-type salami, less strongly flavored -mostly with garlic and eventually paprika- and more heavily smoked than Italian salami. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of German salami such as cervelatwurst. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Chorizo and similar, i.e. a dry pork sausage of Spanish origin made of meat coarsely cut, smoked, highly spiced and having a size similar to large frankfurters. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Ripened kolbasz, also known as dried kolbasz or dried kielbasa or dried knackwurst, i.e. a cured, ripened, spiced sausage, often smoked. For the cured unripened variants of kolbasz use the code A024T 'Fresh kolbasz'. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of sausages cooked during the production process. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Liver-type sausage, such as liverwurst. It usually consists of relevant proportions of finely ground pork or beef livers, seasoned with onions and spices; it may also be smoked after cooking or may include smoked meat such as bacon. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Sliceable or firm cooked sausages. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Polish-type cooked sausage such as Polish smoked sausage which usually consists of pork, salt, pepper, garlic and optional marjoram. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Mortadella-type sausage, which is a product originated in Bologna, Italy. It is made of cured beef and pork, finely ground, with seasonings similar to frankfurters, fully cooked and ready to serve; it is available in rings, rolls or slices of varying diameters. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Bologna-type sausage, such as párizsi, pariser or bologna sausage. It is a cooked sausage inspired to mortadella, but often smoked or with other taste variants. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Blood sausage, for example made from diced, cooked fat, finely ground cooked meat, and gelatin-producing materials mixed with blood and spices. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Cooked salami, usually made from fresh meats, which are cured, stuffed in casings and then cooked in the smokehouse at high temperatures. Cooked salamis can be air dried for a short time, they have a softer texture than dry and semi-dry sausages and they must be refrigerated. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Blood and tongue sausage, for example made from cooked lamb, beef or pork tongues and blood sausage mixtures. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Head cheese such as brawn or sulze or presswurst or presskopf, usually made from chopped, cured pork head meat in a gelatin base. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Frankfurt-type sausage. Frankfurters are traditionally made from pork and beef, but nowadays chicken and turkey are also used. The sizes range from big dinner frankfurters to tiny cocktail size and may be skinless or with natural casings. The terms "frankfurter," "wiener" and "hot dog" are often used interchangeably. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of Frankfurt sausage, a product originated in Frankfurt, Germany, which consists of a combination of beef and pork or only beef. It is cured, smoked and fully cooked and usually it is served hot. Its seasonings may include coriander, garlic, ground mustard, nutmeg, salt, sugar and white pepper. The sizes range from big dinner frankfurters to tiny cocktail size and may be skinless or with natural casings. The terms "frankfurter," "wiener" and "hot dog" are often used interchangeably. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.

The group includes any type of sausage marketed as Wiener or Vienna sausage, which is similar to frankfurter but usually made only from pork, smaller in diameter and softer in texture. The term 'Vienna sausage' most often applied to small, open end sausages packed in cans of water, and it may also be used interchangeably with 'wiener' or 'frankfurter'. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of pâté (i.e. a spreadable paste) made from pork liver. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of bivalve molluscs belonging to the ISSCAAP group 54: mussels. Bivalve molluscs of the family Mytilidae.
Cephalopods classified under the species Octopus vulgaris Lam., commonly known as common octopus.

Cephalopods classified under the taxonomic groups Loligo forbesi Steensrup or Loligo vulgaris Lam. or Loligo spp. or Alloteuthis subulata lam. or Ommastrephes sagittatus Lam. or Todarodes sagittatus Lam. or Todarodes pacificus or Illex illecebrosus or Illex spp., commonly known as Squids.
Cephalopods classified under the species Loligo forbesi Steenstrup, commonly known as Common squid.
The group includes any type of Fish fingers, breaded, including fish fillet.
The group includes any type of Smoked salmon.
The group includes any type of Smoked herring.
The group includes any type of Cream with other ingredients. The added ingredients or flavouring may be considered as minor ingredient.
The group includes any type of Flavoured milk, i.e. milk containing sweetening and flavouring ingredients.
The group includes any type of plain sour cream (without addition of other ingredients) such as creme fraiche or smetana.

foodex2_name: Créme fraiche and other mild variants of sour cream
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Créme fraiche and other mild variants of sour cream.
The group includes any type of Flavoured sour cream. Flavouring may be considered minor ingredient.
The group includes any type of Yoghurt.
The group includes any type of Yoghurt made from cow milk.
The group includes any type of plain yoghurt (without addition of other ingredients) made from cow milk.
The group includes any type of flavoured Yoghurt made from cow milk. Flavouring may be considered minor ingredient.

foodex2_name: Yoghurt drinks, including sweetened and/or flavoured variants
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Yoghurt drinks (liquid consistency), including sweetened and/or flavoured variants. Flavouring may be considered as minor ingredient.
The group includes any type of Traditional sour milk products.
The group includes any type of Kefir.

The group includes any type of Filmjölk (also known as fil or the older word surmjölk), a Nordic mesophilic fermented milk product that is made by fermenting cow's milk with a variety of bacterium from the species Lactococcus lactis and Leuconostoc mesenteroides The bacteria metabolize lactose, the sugar naturally found in milk, into lactic acid. The acid gives filmjölk a sour taste and causes proteins in the milk, mainly casein, to coagulate, thus thickening the final product. The bacteria also produce a limited amount of diacetyl, which gives filmjölk its characteristic taste. Filmjölk is similar to cultured buttermilk, kefir, or yoghurt in consistency, but fermented by different bacteria and thus has a slightly different taste. Compared with yoghurt, filmjölk tastes less sour.

The group includes Viili (Finnish viili, Swedish fil), a type of yoghurt (a mesophilic fermented milk) that originated in the Nordic countries. It has a ropey, gelatinous consistency and a sour taste resulting from lactic acid. This cultured milk product is the results of microbial action of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and a surface-growing yeast-like fungus Geotrichum candidum present in milk, which forms a velvet-like surface on viili. In addition, most traditional viili cultures also contain yeast strains such as Kluveromyces marxianus and Pichia fermentans. The LAB identified in viili including Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris, Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis biovar. diacetylactis, Leuconostoc mesenteroides subsp. cremoris. Among those mesophilic LAB strains, the slime-forming Lc. lactis subsp. cremoris produce a phosphate-containing heteropolysaccharide, named viilian.
The group includes any type of Dairy desserts spoonable.
The group includes any type of Custard, such as Creme anglais and Pastry cream. A custard is a liquid thickened or set by the coagulation of egg protein.

The group includes any type of Starchy pudding. A starch pudding usually consists of milk (or similar), sugar (or similar) and other ingredients, and is thickened with starch or other thickening agent. For example Cornstarch pudding or blanc mange are included in this group.
The group includes any type of Ice cream, milk-based (no milk-imitate-based).

The group includes any type of Cheese and some additional products similar to cheese, like mascarpone and clotted cream. Cheese is produced through the coagulation of milk protein (casein), which is separated from the milk’s whey.
The group includes any type of Fresh uncured cheese and some additional products similar to cheese, such as ricotta and clotted cream, which are ready for consumption shortly after their production.
The group includes any type of Cottage cheese, i.e. a product obtained by cutting and draining a curd. The process includes often washing of the cheese grains to reduce acidity.
The group includes any type of Mozzarella, a stretched soft cheese.
The group includes any type of Quark and fromage frais, which are soft creamy unripened cheeses.
The group includes any type of Clotted Cream.
The group includes any type of Mizithra cheese, a fresh cheese made from milk and whey derived from sheep, goats, cows or mixtures of milks.
The group includes any type of Cream cheese, a fresh cheese with creamy texture, such as philadelfia or boursin.
The group includes any type of Soft brined cheese similar to Feta.
The group includes any type of Feta cheese, a traditional soft brined cheese typical from Greece.
The group includes any type of Telemea cheese, a soft/semi-soft brined cheese.
The group includes any type of firm brined cheese such as ricotta salata type.
The group includes any type of Soft - ripened cheese.
The group includes any type of brie cheese, a type of soft-ripened cheese with bloomy rind (white mould).
The group includes any type of camembert cheese, a type of soft-ripened cheese with bloomy rind (white mould).

foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Soft-ripened cheese veined with blue mould, such as Blue bavarian, blue de graven and similar.

The group includes any type of turunmaa cheese, a type of Firm/semi-hard cheese.

The group includes any type of cheddar cheese, a type of hard cheese.
The group includes any type of emmental cheese, a type of hard cheese.
The group includes any type of gruyere cheese, a type of hard cheese.
The group includes any type of kefalotyri cheese, a type of hard cheese.
The group includes any type of caciocavallo cheese, a type of extra hard cheese.
The group includes any type of comte cheese, a type of extra hard cheese.
The group includes any type of grana padano cheese, a type of extra hard cheese.
The group includes any type of parmigiano reggiano cheese, a type of extra hard cheese.
The group includes any type of pecorino romano cheese, a type of extra hard cheese.
The group includes any type of buche de chevre cheese, a type of bloomy (white mould) or washed rind cheese.
The group includes any type of Firm-ripened cheese with added herbs, spices or other ingredients.

The group includes any type of Processed cheese, spreadable. The ingredients added to melt and eventually flavour the product may be considered minor ingredients.
The group includes any type of Processed cheese wedges and similar. The ingredients added to melt and eventually flavour the product may be considered minor ingredients.

The group includes any type of Bitter chocolate, such as Dark chocolate and Plain chocolate, usually containing at least 35 % total dry cocoa solids, with no milk or much less than milk chocolate and with no sugar or small amount of sugar.
The group includes any type of Bitter-sweet chocolate, a bitter chocolate with small amount of sugar added.

The group includes any type of Milk chocolate, i.e. a sweet chocolate obtained from cocoa products, sugars and milk or milk products. According to EU legislation (Directive 2000/36/EC) milk chocolate has to contain not less than 14 % dry milk solids and not less than 3.5 % milk fat.

The group includes any type of Cream Chocolate. According to EU legislation (Directive 2000/36/EC) Cream chocolate has a higher milk fat content (minimum milk fat content of 5.5 %) than the standard milk chocolate.
The group includes any type of Filled chocolate, e.g. chocolate with nuts or chocolate with raisins and many other types of filling / inclusions.
The group includes any type of Chocolate coated confectionery, apart from the different bars present on the market and coated with chocolate that are included in a specific bar group.
The group includes any type of Pralines, usually consisitng of a chocolate-based productc in a single-mouthful size.
The group includes any type of hard candies, usually cooked-sugar based.
The group includes any type of Marzipan, usually made from sugar or honey, ground almonds and possibly other ingredients.
The group includes any type of Caramel, soft, used as filling or as topping.
The group includes any type of Foamed sugar products, such as marshmallows.
The group includes any type of liquorice candies, such as black licorice or liqorice allsorts.
The group includes any type of Gum drops, usually with jelly/chewy texture, dome shaped and coated in granulated sugar.
The group includes any type of Jelly candies, i.e. gelatin-based candies sold in a variety of shapes and colors (e.g. gummy bear).
The group includes any type of Chewing gum, i.e. a confectionery product with the characteristic of being chewed but not swallowed.
The group includes any type of dessert based on flavoured gelatin.
The group includes any type of fat emulsions and blended fats.
The group includes butter, i.e. a fat emulsion obtained from dairy cream (cultured or not) by churning or equivalent technologies.

The group includes fat-based emulsion resembling in the aspect butter but normally not including significant amounts dairy fat. The fat sources are usually vegetable fats, though historically animal fats including dairy fats have been used. The basic process is emulsifying a blend of vegetable oils and fats, which can be modified using fractionation, interesterification, and/or hydrogenation. The term traditional margarine refers here to the types more solid, most often used for cooking, baking or frying.
The group includes margarines blended with vegetable oils, in many cases leading to spreadable products, used for consumption as such, on bread or similar.
The group includes blends of butter with margarine or oils/fats. These are relatively popular in some countries, particularly for direct use on bread or similar.
The group includes Shortening and similar baking fats, i.e. any fat (or mixture of fats) that is solid at room temperature and used to make pastry.
The group includes fat emulsions and/or fats with added functional substances like omega 3, phytosterols. All margarines and spreadable fat mixes including functional substances are included.
The group includes blends of oils specifically taylored in their formulation and production to be suitable for frying, optimising the frying process and reducing the undesirable process contaminants.
The group includes any type of juice made from Apple.
The group includes any type of juice made from Pineapple.
The group includes any type of juice made from Lemon.
The group includes any type of juice made from Grape including the must separated by peel and seeds used for wine production and consumed as such in some countries.
The group includes any type of juice made from Orange.
The group includes any type of fruit juice obtained from more than one fruit.
The group includes any type of Juice from mixed fruit.
The group includes any type of juice made from Apricot and Orange.

foodex2_name: Fruit nectars (min. 25-50% fruit as defined in EU legislation)
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Fruit nectar, which is a product containing min. 25-50 % fruit juice and/or purée as defined by EU legislation (Council Directive 2001/112/EC). Fruit nectars are obtained by adding water, with or without the addition of sugars and/or honey, to fruit juice or fruit purée and/or concentrated fruit juice or fruit purée and/or to a mixture of those products.
The group includes any type of nectar made from Apple.
The group includes any type of nectar made from Orange.
The group includes any type of nectar made from Peach.
The group includes any type of fruit nectars made from mixed fruit.
The group includes any product obtained by concentrating (reducing the water content of) fruit juices products which may contain or not fibers or particles.
The group includes any type of Juice concentrate made from orange.
The group includes any type of juice made from tomato.
The group includes any type of Fruit smoothie, usually made from fruit and other ingredients such as water, dairy products, sweeteners.
The group includes any type of juice with added vitamins.
The group includes any type of Flavoured bottled water.
Group/item including e.g. Soda Pop or Fizzy drink. The group includes any type of Soft drinks.

foodex2_name: Soft drink, with fruit juice (fruit content below the minimum for nectars)
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Soft drink with fruit juice, i.e. drinks with minor amounts of fruit (below the minimum for nectars). For example Lemonade made of lemon juice and water is included in this group.
The group includes any type of fruit soft drink with minor amounts of Orange.
The group includes any type of Fruit soft drink with minor amounts of mixed fruit.
The group includes any type of flavoured soft drink, not containing fruit pulp or juice.
The group includes any type of soft drink with flavoured with herbs.
The group includes any type of soft drink with lemon flavour.
The group includes any type of soft drink with mixed flavours.
The group includes any type of soft drink with orange flavour.
The group includes any type of soft drinks with cola flavour, usually sweetened and carbonated. Though by default cola beverages are with caffeine, also the variants without caffeine are included.
The group includes any type of Cola beverage containing caffeine.
The group includes any type of Cola Mix flavoured cola, i.e. a soft drink made by mixing a fruit-flavored syrup into cola, such as Cherry cola.

foodex2_name: Diet soft drinks with fruit juice
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Diet soft drinks with fruit juice, such as sugar-free soft drinks with fruit juice.
The group includes any type of Diet soft drinks with flavours, such as sugar-free flavoured soft drinks.
The group includes any type of Diet cola beverage with caffeine.
The group includes any type of Functional drinks, such as energy drinks and isotonic drinks.
The group includes any type of Energy drinks, non-alcoholic functional beverages usually containing caffeine and other ingredients such as vitamins and taurine.
The group includes any type of isotonic and sport drinks, i.e. functional drinks containing electrolytes, carbohydrates, amino acids or proteins.
The group includes any type of Fortified bottled water.

foodex2_name: Liquid drink bases (including concentrates and home-made preparations)
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Liquid drink bases (including concentrates and home-made preparations) usually intended to be diluted with water to produce a beverage. For example Cordial liquid concentrate, Squash, Fruit cordial and Fruit syrup are included in this group. However liquid concentrates used to prepare hot drinks (e.g. tea and herbal liquid extracts, liquid coffee concentrate) are excluded from this group and should be coded with their proper FoodEx2 code.
The group includes any type of Cocoa powder obtained from cacao beans.

The group includes any type of beverage-preparation powder with cocoa, i.e. powdered mix usually containing powdered cocoa and other ingredients (like milk components, sugar, flavourings) intended to be diluted with hot liquids like milk or water to prepare a cocoa-based hot drink. This term should not be confused with A03HG 'Cocoa powder'.

Group/item belonging to the taxonomic group Camellia sinensis (L.) O. Kuntze L. and Thea sinensis L. including e.g. black tea or earl grey or orange pekoe or breakfast tea. The group includes any type of Tea leaves and stalks, fermented.

foodex2_name: Tea leaves and stalks with fruit and flavours
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Tea leaves and stalks with added fruit and flavours.
The group includes any type of Herbal infusion materials as defined in the pesticide regulation.

foodex2_name: Herbal infusion materials from leaves and herbs
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of herbal infusion materials obtained from leaves and herbs as defined in EU pesticide regulation.
The group includes any type of Cocoa beverages, i.e. beverages usually made with cocoa powder and possibly other cocoa-based products dissolved into a liquid.
The group includes any type of Hot chocolate, i.e. a heated beverage made from cocoa powder dissolved into hot milk or water.
The group includes any type of Tea beverages, i.e. beverages usually made with tea leaves derivatives or tea-based ingredients (Camellia sinensis) and water or another liquid.
The group includes any type of Fermented tea infusion (e.g. black tea infusion), i.e. a beverage prepared with hot water and fermented tea leaves.
The group includes any type of Non-fermented tea infusion (green and white tea infusions), i.e. a beverage prepared with hot water and non-fermented tea leaves.
The group includes any type of decaffeinated (caffeine-free) tea infusion, i.e. a beverage prepared with hot water and decaffeinated tea leves.

foodex2_name: Tea infusion with added flavouring ingredients
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Tea infusion with added flavouring ingredients (e.g. bergamot, spearmint, vanilla).
The group includes any type of Herbal and other non-tea infusions.
The group includes any type of Camomile (Chamomile) infusion.
The group includes any type of Fruit infusion.
The group includes any type of Lime blossoms infusion.
The group includes any type of Lemon verbena infusion.
The group includes any type of Rooibos infusion.
The group includes any type of Beer, an alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of malt (or other saccharine substance), flavoured with hops or other aromatic bitter ingredients.
The group includes any type of lager beer (ferments under cold conditions).
The group includes any type of strong beer such as Bockbeer.
The group includes any type of regular beer such as Kölsch or Lager or Pils or Export or Alt.
The group includes any type of light beer, i.e. beer with reduced alcohol content.
The group includes any type of alcohol-free beer.
The group includes any type of ale beer (usually ferments under warm conditions).
The group includes any type of pale ale beer, usually a top-fermented beer.
The group includes any type of dark ale beer.

The group includes any type of stout beer. Stout is a dark beer made using roasted malt or roasted barley, hops, water and yeast. Stouts were traditionally the generic term for the strongest or stoutest porters, typically 7% or 8% produced by a brewery.
The group includes any type of wheat beer, a beer brewed with a large proportion of wheat such as the Weissbier.
The group includes any type of Beer-like beverages such as Malt drink and Malt beer.
The group includes any type of Shandy, a mixture of beer and fizzy lemonade.
The group includes any type of mixed beer drinks such as Chiefly.
The group includes any type of Fortified and liqueur wines, i.e. wines with added alcoholic ingredients.
The group includes any type of Liqueurs, i.e. alcoholic beverages that has been flavored with fruit, herbs, nuts, spices, flowers, or cream and bottled with added sugar.
The group includes any type of Mixed alcoholic drinks such as alcoholic cocktails.
The group includes any type of Cocktail drink.
The group includes any type of supplements based on vitamins and minerals, excluding those claimed for sporting people and the carbohydrate-electrolyte solutions, addressed by a specific group.
The group includes all supplements based only on vitamins.
The group includes all supplements based only on minerals (normally salts of different chemical elements).

foodex2_name: Combination of vitamin and mineral only supplements
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes all supplements based only on formulations including both minerals (normally salts of different chemical elements) and vitamins.

foodex2_name: Formulations containing special fatty acids (e.g. Omega-3, essential fatty acids)
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of supplements/nutraceuticals containing special fatty acids (e.g. omega-3, essential fatty acids). Medium-Chain Triglycerides (MCT), often consumed by sporting people are also included in this group.
The group includes any type of Protein and amino acids supplements. Branched Chain Amino Acids (BCAA), often consumed by sporting people are also included in this group.
The group includes any type of Meat imitates and substitutes.
The group includes any type of Soyabean-based meat imitates i.e.  meat substitutes which main ingredient is soy, e.g. soy sausages, balls, schnitzels, soy mince, burger patties.
The group includes any type of Fungi-based meat imitates, such as quorn.
The group includes any type of Milk imitates and substitutes, i.e. liquid products meant to replace the milk from a mammal.
The group includes any type of Soya drink, often sold as milk substitute.
The group includes any type of Oats drink, often sold as milk substitute.
The group includes any type of Rice drink, often sold as milk substitute.
The group includes any type of dairy imitates and substitutes, other than milks, i.e. food items resembling dairy products but not derived from mammal milk.
The group includes any type of Imitation cream, i.e. a product resembling a dairy cream but not derived from mammal milk such as creams derived from a plant source.

The group includes any type of non-dairy coffee creamers, i.e. products intended to substitute for milk or cream as an additive to coffee, tea or other beverages. They are usually without lactose, but often containing milk-derived protein.
The group includes any type of Tofu, also known as soy curd, i.e. a product usually made from soybeans, water and coagulants.
The group includes any type of soya yoghurt, i.e. a yogurt made from soy drink.
The group includes any type of Imitation cheese, i.e. a product resembling a cheese but not derived from mammal milk.

The category covers all type of dishes containing more than one characterising ingredient and having a recipe behind them where the ingredients are so diverse that no relevant main category can be identified.
The group includes any type of Potato based dishes, i.e. composite dishes in which the principal characterising ingredient is potato.
The group includes any type of Potato casserole, a potato-based dish usually cooked in the oven in a casserole pan.
The group includes any type of Prepared potato salad.
The group includes any type of composite dish based on Potatoes and cheese.
The group includes any type of Legumes based dishes, i.e. composite dishes in which the principal characterising ingredient is a legume.
The group includes any type of Meat based dishes, i.e. composite dishes in which the principal characterising ingredient is meat.
The group includes any type of Goulash, a traditional Hungarian dish based on stewed meat and vegetables, and highly spiced with paprika and other spices.
The group includes any type of Meat stew, i.e. meat-based dishes prepared by stewing (by slowly cooking) meat with other ingredients.
The group includes any type of Meat loaf, i.e. composite dishes usually made from ground meat and other ingredients formed into a loaf shape.
The group includes any type of Moussaka, an eggplant and meat based dish of the Balkans, Eastern Mediterranean, and the Middle East. The best known variation outside the region is the Greek moussaka.
The group includes any type of Meat burger (no sandwich), i.e. patties of ground meat.
The group includes any type of Meat balls, usually made from ground meat and other ingredients shaped as small balls.
The group includes any type of Fish and seafood based dishes, i.e. composite dishes in which the principal characterising ingredient is fish or seafood.
The group includes any type of Fish pâté, a composite fish-based dish usually with a finely ground texture.
The group includes any type of Vegetable based dishes, i.e. composite dishes in which the principal characterising ingredient is a vegetable.
The group includes any type of Vegetable casserole, a vegetable-based dish usually cooked in the oven in a casserole pan.
The group includes any type of Mixed vegetables, braised.
The group includes any type of Mixed vegetables, boiled.
The group includes any type of gratinated Vegetables, i.e. composite vegetable-based dishes characterised by a browned/golden crust.
The group includes any type of Ratatouille, a composite dish based on stewed vegetables.
The group includes any type of Egg based dishes, i.e. composite dishes in which the principal characterising ingredient is egg.

The group includes any type of quiche. In French cuisine, a quiche is an oven-baked dish usually made with eggs, milk or cream and other ingredients (e.g. vegetables, meat products, etc.) in a pastry crust.
The group includes any type of Sandwich and sandwich-like dishes.
The group includes any type of Sandwich with processed meat (e.g. ham) topping/filling.

foodex2_name: Sandwich with meat and vegetable topping/filling
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Sandwich with meat and vegetable topping/filling.
The group includes any type of Hamburger sandwich, i.e. hamburger meat with bread.

The group includes any type of Pizza and pizza-like dishes. Pizza like dishes include pies and other topped/filled cereal dough bases (normally from doughs other than bread dough) cooked after topping/filling.

foodex2_name: Pizza and similar with cheese topping
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Pizza with cheese topping.

foodex2_name: Pizza and similar with processed meat topping
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Pizza with processed meat (e.g. ham) topping.

foodex2_name: Pizza and similar with cheese, meat, mushrooms, and vegetables
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Pizza with cheese, meat, mushrooms and vegetables.

The group includes any type of Finger food. In Europe and other regions, finger food means a product intended to be eaten with hands (and not using cutlery) and it is often an appetizer or entree. Sausage rolls, spring rolls, vol au vents and canapé are included in this category.
The group includes any type of Sausage roll, usually made of puff pastry and sausage.

foodex2_name: Pastas and rice (or other cereal) –based dishes
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Pasta and rice (or other cereal) –based dishes.
The group includes any type of Pasta based dishes already cooked.
The group includes any type of Lasagna, i.e. a dish made of layers of flat-shaped pasta alternated with sauces and other ingredients.
The group includes any type of Pasta, cooked, with mixed sauce.
The group includes any type of Rice based dishes cooked.

The group includes any type of Dolma, i.e. a variety of stuffed vegetable dishes in the Greek cuisine, cuisines of the former Ottoman Empire and surrounding regions such as Russia, Iran and the Caucasus and Central and South Asia. Perhaps the best-known is the grape-leaf dolma. Common vegetables to stuff include onion, zucchini, eggplant, tomato and pepper. The stuffing may or may not include meat. Meat dolmas are generally served warm, often with sauce; meatless ones are generally served cold, though meatless dolmas are eaten both ways in Iran. Both are often eaten with yogurt.
The group includes any type of Risotto, a typical Italian dish based on rice and different types of sauces.
The group includes any type of composite dish based on Rice and vegetables.
The group includes any type of composite dish based on Rice, meat, and vegetables.
The group includes any type of Soups, ready for consumption bought as such or prepared from ingredients as a recipe.
The group includes any type of Tomato soup.
The group includes any type of Legume (beans) soup.
The group includes any type of Mixed vegetables soup.
The group includes any type of Meat/poultry soup.
The group includes any type of Meat and vegetable soup.

foodex2_name: Cereal products and grains based soup
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Cereal products and grains based soup, included those with rice, pasta, dumplings, spelt, etc.
The group includes any type of Milk product/egg soup.
The group includes any type of Fruit soup.
The group includes any type of Salads.
The group includes any type of Mixed green salad, i.e. salads made with leafy vegetables.
The group includes any type of Mixed vegetable salad, i.e. salads made with different types of vegetables.
The group includes any type of Greek salad, i.e. a salad usually made with tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, feta cheese, and olives.
The group includes any type of Prepared mixed egg/meat/fish/vegetable salad, usually bound with mayonnaise.
The group includes any type of seasoning composed by many different ingredients, such as miso.
The group includes any type of Mixed herbs and spices.
The group includes any type of Curry powder, a spice mix typical in Asian cuisine.
The group includes any type of stock cubes or granulate (bouillon base) usually used to prepare bouillons (broths).
The group includes any type of chicken stock cubes or granulate.
The group includes any type of beef stock cubes or granulate.
The group includes any type of vegetable stock cubes or granulate.
The group includes any type of savoury extracts obtained from undefined commodities of plant origin.
The group includes any type of savoury extracts obtained from meat.
The group includes any type of Gravy instant granules.
The group includes any type of Savoury sauces.
The group includes any type of Bechamel sauce, i.e. a milk-based souce with a roux (butter and flour) as thickening component
The group includes any type of sauce based on cheese.

foodex2_name: Continental european brown cooked sauce, gravy
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Continental European brown sauce or gravy, such as stock meat brown sauce, gravy, Espagnole sauce. These sauces are usually based on meat stock and similar meat-based ingredients. This term should not be confused with British islands brown sauce which is mainly made with tomatoes, molasses, vinegar and other ingredients not obtained by meat products.
The group includes any type of sauce based on dairy cream.
The group includes any type of Tomato-containing cooked sauce, i.e. sauces made by cooking tomatoes with or without other major ingredients, such as meat, mushrooms, dairy, eggs.
The group includes any type of sauce made by cooking vegetables.
The group includes any type of Mustard sauce, eventually with different ingredients. Mustard is usually a sauce based on mustard seeds (black, white, brown mustard) mixed with other ingredients.
The group includes any type of sweet mustard sauce (sweet flavor).
The group includes any type of mild mustard sauce (mild flavor, less pungent flavor).
The group includes any type of Vinegar.
The group includes any type of Vinegar made from wine.
The group includes any type of Vinegar made from applea.
The group includes any type of Tomato ketchup (typically made from tomatoes, a sweetener, vinegar) and derived sauces.
The group includes any type of Tabasco sauce, i.e. a sauce based on tabasco peppers.
The group includes any type of Soy sauce (Soya sauce, Tamari), made from fermented soybeans and other ingredients.
The group includes any type of Mayonnaise sauce, usually made with vegetable oil and egg yolk.
The group includes any type of low-fat mayonnaise (light).
The group includes any type of Curry sauce, also known as curry paste.
The group includes any type of Hollandaise type sauce, such as bernaise sauce, usually made of butter and egg yolk.

foodex2_name: Mixed and other not listed condiments
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Mixed and other not listed condiments.
The group includes any type of Salad dressing.
The group includes any type of Tartar sauce.
The group includes any type of Mixed pickle.
The group includes any type of Relish, i.e. a product made with cooked and pickled vegetables or fruits, typically used as a condiment.
The group includes different types of balsamic vinegar, an aromatic aged vinegar, and its flavoured variants.
The group includes any type of Popped cereals made by popping/puffing cereal grains.
The group includes any type of Processed (preserved) tomato products.

The group includes any type of processed whole meat products, i.e. cured meat cuts made of entire pieces of muscle meat. They can include relevant portions of fat tissues. The eventual removal of not edible parts is unspecified.
The group includes any type of Other fresh uncured cheeses.
The category covers any type of Confectionery including chocolate.
The group includes any type of Vegetable juices.
The group includes any type of Unsweetened spirits and liqueurs.

The group includes any type of processed cereal flakes similar to corn flakes, i.e. breakfast cereals usually obtained by soaking-cooking/steaming, pressing, drying and flaking cereal grains/flours mixed with admixture of additional ingredients (e.g. sweeteners).
The group includes blends of different fats/oils or of different fats/oils with margarines or butter
The group includes any type of halloumi, a Cypriot semi-hard, unripened brined cheese made from a mixture of goat's and sheep's milk, and sometimes also cow's milk. Often consumed fried or grilled.

The group includes a range of snack-type (usually sweet) products derived principally from dairy products like cheese, milk fillings etc. Examples of these are cheese curd rolls, kinder chocolate, fetta al latte, milchschnitte, Turo rudi.
The group includes any type of Corned beef, cooked.

The group includes any type of special bread, i.e. bread containing particular ingredients and additives which ensure a shelf-life longer than that of regular bread. In this group are included breads baked in a mold intended to be sliced for preparing sandwiches and hamburger roll-type breads with extended shelf-life. Similar breads with normal composition and/or with a shelf-life like regular bread are not included in this term and should be coded as regular bread.
The group includes any type of fruit and/or vegetable juice and nectar.
The group includes dairy imitates and substitutes, i.e. products that are used to replace dairy-milk in the human diet, made with non-dairy ingredients.
The group includes any type of bread with a soft sponge-like structure due to leavening.
The group includes any type of Fruit juice, which is a product 100% obtained from a fruit.

The group includes any type of plain wafers (i.e. without inclusions, fillings or coatings) and wafer-based biscuits. For example wafer and cream sandwich cookies (e.g. Neapolitan wafers), ice-cream cones made of wafer and Raffaello-type sweets are included in this group.
The group includes any type of Potato crisps from potato slices.
The group includes any type of Potato crisps from potato-based dough.
The group includes any type of French fries from cut potato.

The group includes Seafood (any non-mammal, non-fish marine animal) products canned or jarred (as preserves or semi-preserves). Otherwise the product is intended by default to be fully preserved (e.g. retorting).
The group includes any type of meat stock cubes or granulate.
The group includes any type of Mixed vegetables soup, clear (without pieces). Otherwise known under the name Vegetable bouillon.

foodex2_name: Mixed vegetables soup, with puree or pieces
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Mixed vegetables soup, with puree or pieces.
The group includes any type of Meat soup, with meat pieces.
The group includes any type of Meat soup, clear (without meat pieces). Otherwise known under the name Meat bouillon.

foodex2_name: Meat and vegetable soup, with puree or pieces
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of Meat and vegetable soup, with puree or pieces.

The group includes any type of potato puree, i.e. a composite food in general produced from potatoes and often dairy ingredients, fat and salt, with possibly some flavouring ingredients. It may be produced from boiled potatoes or reconstituted from powdered (or flaked) ingredients with addition of milk or other liquid. Here it is considered in the ready to eat form.

The group includes any type of potato puree produced from boiled potatoes and often dairy ingredients, fat and salt, with possibly some flavouring ingredients. Here it is considered in the ready to eat form.

The group includes Spreadable chocolate products based on cacao ingredients, different types of fats and very often nut derivatives. For example chocolate-hazelnut spread like nutella and other similar brands are included in this group.
The group includes any type of pasta dish with different sauces, based on plain (not stuffed) pasta.

The group includes any type of Pie and tart-type pastry (either small, used as finger food, or larger) with savoury (vegetable and-or meat and-or cheese) filling. For example Erbazzone, Vegetable pie and Meat pie are included in this group.
The group includes any type of crisp bread, i.e. a flat and dry type of bread similar to crackers, but tendentially harder. It traditionally contains rye flour, but nowadays also wheat flour.

The group includes any type of Freshly-made cheese curd, with no ripening or salting, just a variable degree of draining and heating. Available in different forms and under different names in many central-european countries such as Turo, Curdled milk, Biezpiens and Milk curd. Very similar to home made cottage cheese, possibly more acidic.
The group includes any type of chocolate, i.e. solid product obtained by refining, conching and tempering mixtures of cocoa mass, cocoa butter and eventually other ingredients.

foodex2_name: Soft drinks with minor amounts of fruits or flavours
foodex2_scope_note: The group includes any type of soft drink with minor amounts of fruits or flavours, i.e. drinks with flavours, sweetening ingredients and, in the case of fruit tasting sorts, with relatively small amounts of fruit. These drinks are mostly carbonated.
The group includes different types of candies, with hard or soft texture.
The group includes any type of formulated products where chocolate or cocoa is the major component (in terms of amount or characterisation), like pralines and other chocolate bonbons.
The group includes any type of thin-fried slices or sticks of potatoes, or similar crunchy products obtained by cereal doughs or vegetables, used as snack.
The group includes any type of french beans (green Phaseolus vulgaris cultivars) canned or jarred.
Product known as porridge obtained by boiling or by soaking rolled, crushed, or steel cut grains or other cereal meals in water. Other ingredients can possibly be added.

The group includes any type of canned/jarred vegetables, i.e. Plant commodities used as vegetables, canned or jarred (as preserves or semi-preserves) in order to extend their shelf-life. Otherwise the product is intended by default to be fully preserved (e.g. retorting).
The group includes any type of Fish products canned or jarred (as preserves or semi-preserves). Otherwise the product is intended by default to be fully preserved (e.g. retorting).
The group includes Fish products preserved by smoking. Smoking of fish is either cold (smoke temperatures around 20–30°C) or hot (smoke temperatures around 60–80°C).
The group includes any type of Fish products preserved by effect of salt.
The group includes any type of Fish products marinated with acidic and or spiced media.
The group includes products known as porridge obtained by boiling or by soaking rolled, crushed, or steel cut grains or other cereal meals in milk. Other ingredients can possibly be added.

The group includes products known as porridge obtained by boiling or by soaking rolled, crushed, or steel cut grains or other cereal meals in water, milk, or both. Other ingredients can possibly be added.
The group includes any type of emulsified oil and egg based sauces such as mayonnaise, hollandaise and related sauces
The group includes any type of White sauce, such as Bechamel sauce, butter sauce, velouté mother sauce etc.

The group includes any type of Extruded breakfast cereal products, i.e. shaped (rings, balls etc.) extruded cereals with eventual admixture of additional ingredients (e.g. flavourings and sweeteners).
The group includes any type of Canned tunas and similar.
The group includes any type of Canned anchovies.
The group includes any type of Salt-preserved cod. Very common in the past, now also replaced by other white fishes.
Bivalve molluscs classified under the species Mytilus edulis, commonly known as Blue mussel.
The group includes any type of Sauces based on meat and without tomato or only very minor tomato proportion, such as white ragu
The group includes any type of Smoked mackerel.
The group includes any type of composite dishes based on bread or similar products. For example dumplings made from bread (Bread dumplings) served without broth are included in this group.
The group includes any type of Phyllo or filo dough, a very thin unleavened dough commonly used for making pastries such as baklava.
They can be closed or open-faced with no crust on top and in different shapes and forms. In this group are included karelian pasty and Flaouna.
The group includes any type of Mixed vegetables (this code is used for e.g. vegetable mix for soup).

The group includes any type of Strained yoghurt, i.e. yogurt that has been strained to remove its whey, resulting in a thicker consistency than unstrained yogurt. For example Greek yoghurt, Labneh and Yogurt cheese are included in this group.
The group includes any type of Peppermint infusion.
The group includes any type of Fennel infusion.
